items.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: Dick Gibson I think was the first one who really popularized that kind of thing. And unfortunately I never went to any of his parties

ctx.x: said, “Here’s a good way to get some of these interviews is you go and you be there for the three days. And I was amazed that such a thing existed. I sort of didn’t know about it. But I also was amazed at how hip the audience was that came to these things. I just — you don’t expect people to be so informed about the music.

Well don’t forget, don’t forget, we were dealing with the jazz parties with a generation that grew up with the music. I mean these were people, for example, who used to see Ralph Sutton at Sunnie’s Rendezvous in Aspen and who used to see these musicians play in the clubs in New York at the time, you know, the hotels. The hotels had swing music, had jazz music, there were clubs and these were people who grew up with the music just as the later generation grew up with the Beatles, these were people who grew up with…
As a producer of these things, did you ever have to deal with personality conflicts between the musicians?
